original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.

actual_scope: On the selected PR1094 owner map, every directed three-role cycle on three distinct occupied bins that touches a slack-7 bin and strictly majorizes the slack triple fails the selected source-event window list.
scope_change_reason: The card allows one bounded residual of the selected packing. The full T16 search and the single rank transition {0,1,7}->{0,0,8} are already published. This census is the remaining slack-7-touching majorization class, including that transition as a recomputed control.
bottleneck_link: A legal idle-histogram change is what could raise the binding complex primitive. This residual has 32,981,939 capacity-feasible uniform improvements and zero window-legal ones, so it contributes no paid-profile or kappa gain.
stop_rule: Stop after the complete slack-7-anchored three-bin census, its incomparable companion, and the synthetic window control. Do not open a slack-3 anchor search in this session.

open_questions.question: Does any directed three-bin cycle that avoids every slack-7 bin strictly majorize its slack triple and land inside the selected source-event windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The complex primitive still binds. A window-legal majorizing cycle outside this anchor would be a concrete idle-histogram improvement to price.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat this majorization join with the anchor restricted to the 754 roles in slack-3 bins, and reject any triple that also touches slack 7 so the domains stay disjoint.
open_questions.blocked_by: Slack-3 class products are much larger than the slack-7 join, and three-component transitions that are not majorization-ordered still need a separate exact sign rule.
